MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val enableFuzzingExplanation = "Adds a small random variation to review intervals. This prevents cards that were reviewed together from always coming due on the same day, spreading your workload more evenly. MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val fsrsSimpleExplanation = "FSRS (Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler) uses a scientific model of memory to schedule reviews. It tracks two key properties for each card: stability (how long you'll remember it) and difficulty (how hard the card is for you). FSRS calculates the optimal review time to maintain your desired recall rate, adapting to your performance over time."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val fsrsTechnicalDetails = "FSRS uses a memory model based on the forgetting curve:

Retrievability: R = (1 + t/S × factor)^decay

Where S is stability (days until 90% recall), t is time elapsed.

After each review, stability and difficulty are updated using 21 optimized parameters. The model accounts for:
• Memory strength grows more when retrievability is low
• Harder cards gain stability more slowly
• Forgetting (Again) reduces stability based on current difficulty

The optimal interval is calculated to maintain your desired retention rate."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val kadoLiteDescription = "We also developed a Lite version for ESP32 microcontrollers (specifically the ESP32-C6 with Waveshare 1.47\" Touch LCD) so you can study your flashcards on the go with a dedicated device."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val learningStepsExplanation = "When you see a new card for the first time, it goes through learning steps before entering the regular review schedule. Each step defines how long to wait before showing the card again. For example, '1m, 10m' means show the card again after 1 minute, then after 10 minutes, before scheduling a full review."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val maxIntervalExplanation = "The maximum number of days between reviews. Even if the algorithm calculates a longer interval, it will be capped at this value. The default of 36500 days (~100 years) effectively means no limit."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val relearningStepsExplanation = "When you forget a card (rate Again), it enters relearning. These steps work like learning steps but for cards you previously knew. After completing all relearning steps, the card returns to the regular review schedule with adjusted stability."
MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val resetProgressMessage = "All review progress for this deck will be erased. Cards will be treated as new."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val sm2TechnicalDetails = "SM-2 uses an ease factor (EF) that multiplies the previous interval:

• New cards start with EF = 2.5
• Again: resets interval, EF -= 0.2
• Hard: interval × 1.2, EF -= 0.1
• Good: interval × EF
• Easy: interval × EF × 1.3, EF += 0.2

EF is clamped to [1.3, 4.0]. Intervals are clamped to [1, 36500] days."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val statsGuideBodyFsrs = "New — Cards you haven't studied yet.

Learning — Cards going through learning steps (e.g., 1m, 10m) before entering the regular review schedule, or relearning steps after being forgotten.

Young — Cards in the review state with an interval under 21 days. FSRS tracks each card's stability and difficulty to schedule optimal reviews.

Mature — Cards with an interval of 21+ days. These have high memory stability.

Due Now — Total cards ready for review right now (new + overdue)."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EnStrings$override val statsGuideBodySm2 = "New — Cards you haven't studied yet.

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EsStrings$override val fsrsSimpleExplanation = "FSRS (Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler) utiliza un modelo científico de la memoria para programar repasos. Rastrea dos propiedades clave de cada tarjeta: estabilidad (cuánto tiempo la recordarás) y dificultad (qué tan difícil es la tarjeta para ti). FSRS calcula el momento óptimo de repaso para mantener tu tasa de recuerdo deseada, adaptándose a tu rendimiento con el tiempo."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EsStrings$override val fsrsTechnicalDetails = "FSRS usa un modelo de memoria basado en la curva del olvido:

Recuperabilidad: R = (1 + t/S × factor)^decaimiento

Donde S es la estabilidad (días hasta 90% de recuerdo), t es el tiempo transcurrido.

Después de cada repaso, la estabilidad y la dificultad se actualizan usando 21 parámetros optimizados. El modelo considera:
• La fuerza de la memoria crece más cuando la recuperabilidad es baja
• Las tarjetas más difíciles ganan estabilidad más lentamente
• Olvidar (Otra vez) reduce la estabilidad según la dificultad actual

El intervalo óptimo se calcula para mantener tu tasa de retención deseada."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EsStrings$override val maxIntervalExplanation = "El número máximo de días entre repasos. Incluso si el algoritmo calcula un intervalo más largo, se limitará a este valor. El valor predeterminado de 36500 días (~100 años) significa efectivamente sin límite."

MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EsStrings$override val relearningStepsExplanation = "Cuando olvidas una tarjeta (calificas Otra vez), entra en reaprendizaje. MaxLineLength:Strings.kt$EsStrings$override val sm2TechnicalDetails = "SM-2 usa un factor de facilidad (EF) que multiplica el intervalo anterior:

• Las tarjetas nuevas comienzan con EF = 2.5

Maduras — Tarjetas con un intervalo de 21+ días. Tienen alta estabilidad de memoria.

Pendientes — Total de tarjetas listas para repasar ahora (nuevas + atrasadas)."
